beginner.headline: Zelensky Wants More US Help for Ukraine
beginner.brief: Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, spoke to the BBC in Kyiv. He said the US was paying too much attention to the Middle East. He wants the US to push Russia harder during peace talks. The aim of these talks is to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. The latest peace talks made no clear progress. Zelensky said he expected talks to start again in December. Some businesses in Kyiv have closed because power cuts and attacks have made their costs too high. Some people have already left the city for the winter. Zelensky said Ukraine would try to defend its capital.

intermediate.headline: Zelensky Calls for More US Pressure on Russia
intermediate.brief: Ukraine's president, Volodymyr Zelensky, expressed frustration with the US, saying it was not putting enough pressure on Russia during negotiations. He said delays in receiving missiles used to stop other missiles were costing Ukrainian lives. He also complained that the US was focusing on the Middle East and providing more help there. Zelensky said it was strange that Donald Trump had posted a picture showing himself embracing Vladimir Putin and describing him as a friend. The latest negotiations, held with help from a third party in Abu Dhabi, made no clear progress. The talks were expected to resume in December, according to Zelensky. He called for support from allies, countries that help Ukraine, and urged the US to put pressure on Russia. The US says it is neutral, meaning it does not take either side, while seeking a peace agreement that can last. Zelensky reported a serious shortage of defensive missiles and said the US was delaying deliveries of Patriot air defence systems. Russian attacks have become more frequent and deadly, and the number of civilians killed has reached its highest level. Power cuts and attacks on transport networks have raised operating costs so much that some businesses have shut. Zelensky acknowledged that Ukraine was preparing for a difficult and dangerous winter.

advanced.headline: Zelensky Urges Stronger US Pressure as Ukraine's Defences Strain
advanced.brief: Volodymyr Zelensky has accused the US of applying insufficient pressure on Russia and said delays in delivering essential defensive missiles were costing Ukrainian lives. He also criticised Washington's emphasis on the Middle East, arguing that countries there were receiving greater assistance. Zelensky expressed unease over Donald Trump's portrayal of Vladimir Putin as a friend in a post showing the two men embracing. His criticism comes after a period of caution in managing US relations following a bruising Oval Office encounter with Trump in 2025. The report describes the two US envoys seeking a peace deal as appearing more in tune with Moscow's position than Kyiv's. The latest talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi, produced no obvious progress, according to the report. Russia appears to have regressed to its initial hardline positions across the negotiating agenda, judging by its public statements. Zelensky said it remained unclear whether European negotiators would be at the table, despite the US envoys having announced their participation. He urged the US to live up to its reputation for strength and use its influence to push Russia towards results. The US presents its neutrality as part of an effort to secure a peace agreement that can hold. Zelensky said Ukraine could now destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones and that the proportion was improving. He described a severe deficit of interceptors, missiles used to stop incoming ballistic missiles, and accused the US of delaying deliveries of Patriot systems. Zelensky also confirmed that the US satellite communications systems Starlink and Starshield remained restricted in occupied Ukrainian territory. Ukrainian drone units reported that some Russian drones were travelling farther into Ukraine unhindered because their interceptor drones could no longer catch them. Ukraine has increased its long-range strikes on Russian targets, including oil refineries and ships carrying weapons or fuel. While acknowledging that such strikes were highly dangerous, Zelensky said Ukrainian forces never conducted them without coordinating with partners. Zelensky acknowledged that Ukraine was bracing for a difficult and dangerous winter. Some residents had already left town for the winter and businesses had closed as power cuts and attacks on logistics networks pushed operating costs unmanageably high.
